title: The Last Exact Step
statement: A clock wheel and a sea anemone share one head above a borrowed architectural figure. The map and printed theory establish a measured world; a flowering line and departing insect carry its forms beyond that world. The seam is exact, but what continues from it is not: interpretation begins where a structure becomes something to work with rather than merely obey.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent where following an instruction ends and interpreting it begins.

actions.title: The Last Exact Step
actions.statement: A clock wheel and a sea anemone share one head above a borrowed architectural figure. The map and printed theory establish a measured world; a flowering line and departing insect carry its forms beyond that world. The seam is exact, but what continues from it is not: interpretation begins where a structure becomes something to work with rather than merely obey.

notes.note: Begin with a measured map field and a split circular emblem: a clock wheel meets a living rosette at a precise vertical seam. Leave generous paper around the construction.
Give the divided emblem a human body, so the boundary belongs to an interpreter rather than remaining only a diagram. A small airborne insect will carry the circular motif beyond the seam.

Strengthen the figure beneath the shared wheel/flower head, and let a botanical branch pass through the figure’s working space. Interpretation should emerge from handling a structure, not simply occupy its opposite side.

notes.note: The finished composition holds a precise central seam while the flower, figure, and insect move beyond its measured field. The shared radial head makes instruction and interpretation continuous without making them identical. No further edits are needed.
